record.paper_title: Open Problems on Syzygies and Hilbert Functions
record.original_question: For every artinian graded finitely generated S-module M, are the total Betti numbers bounded below by the Koszul ranks, b_i^S(M) >= binomial(n,i) for all i >= 0?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $K$ be a field and $S = K[x_1, \dots, x_n]$ the standard graded polynomial ring in $n$ variables. For a finitely generated graded $S$-module $M$, let
$$b_i^S(M) = \dim_K \mathrm{Tor}_i^S(M, K)$$
denote the $i$-th total Betti number of $M$ (the rank of the $i$-th free module in the minimal graded free resolution of $M$ over $S$).

Assume $M$ is artinian (equivalently, $\dim_K M < \infty$). Determine whether the inequality
$$b_i^S(M) \;\geq\; \binom{n}{i}$$
holds for every $i \geq 0$ and every such artinian graded finitely generated $S$-module $M$.
artifact.status_search_result: This is the Buchsbaum-Eisenbud-Horrocks rank conjecture (pointwise version). The weaker total rank conjecture, that the sum of Betti numbers is at least $2^n$, was proven by Mark Walker (Annals of Math, 2017) for modules of finite projective dimension over local rings containing a field where 2 is invertible. The stronger pointwise bound $b_i \geq \binom{n}{i}$ remains open in general, with only special cases established (e.g., Charalambous–Evans for certain cases, and partial results by Erman and others).

status_evidence.title: Total Betti numbers of modules of finite projective dimension
status_evidence.snippet: Walker proves the sum of Betti numbers is at least 2^n (total rank conjecture) for finite projective dimension modules in char != 2.
status_evidence.claim: Walker resolved the weaker total rank version, but the pointwise BEH rank conjecture remains open.

status_evidence.title: A special case of the Buchsbaum-Eisenbud-Horrocks rank conjecture
status_evidence.snippet: Establishes only a special case of the pointwise rank conjecture, indicating the general statement is unresolved.
status_evidence.claim: The general pointwise inequality b_i >= C(n,i) is still open.
